title: Hybrid sterility can be removed under domestication

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Hybrid sterility can be removed under domestication

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because many domestic animals are believed to descend from two or more distinct species that are now fully fertile together, sterility between species is not indelible but can be removed by domestication.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we must look at sterility, not as an indelible characteristic, but as one capable of being removed by domestication.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VIII, “Hybridism”; section “Sterility various in degree, not universal, affected by close interbreeding, removed by domestication”. Scope: domestic animals derived from several wild species (dogs, cattle)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch08-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Current fertility and ancestry are testable, but Darwin's premise about distinct progenitor species is often uncertain. Existing data only indirectly show that domestication removed an earlier barrier.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For domestic lineages with multiple wild progenitors, compare present cross fertility with wild-source crosses and identify changes associated with domestication. Repeated evolved restoration of fertility supports removability.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Historical ancestral sterility is seldom directly measured.

Many domestic-origin claims involve populations rather than distinct species.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.76

discriminating power: 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Genomes can check the historical premise that particular domestics combine more than one species, and breed databases record present fertility. The variable that would show sterility being removed, a before-and-after barrier between the same lineages, is mostly absent. The test therefore covers a few candidate domestics and does not reach the general mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare intrinsic hybrid sterility between the wild progenitors of a domestic animal with fertility among the domestic descendants supposed to combine those progenitors. Loss of a barrier that is still present in the wild pair would support removal by domestication; barriers that are unchanged, or domestic forms that never had intersterile progenitors, would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fertility of the original wild crosses at the time of domestication is rarely measured.

Several of the multi-species origin stories are themselves uncertain, which confounds the comparison.

Selection on fertility under domestication is hard to separate from hybrid ancestry.
